comment.comment: `#` to end of line. The lexer has no block comment form.
comment.name: comment.line.number-sign.science

string.comment: A string never spans a line break (lexer.rs `fn string`), so `$` is an end alternative and an unterminated literal cannot run away.
string.name: string.quoted.double.science

patterns.comment: The exact set of lexer.rs `fn escape`: n t r 0 backslash double-quote single-quote.
patterns.name: constant.character.escape.science

patterns.comment: One to six hex digits naming a Unicode scalar value.
patterns.name: constant.character.escape.unicode.science

patterns.comment: Anything else after a backslash is SC0006.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.unknown-escape.science

unit-literal.comment: `9.8<m/s^2>`, per unit-literals.md. Anchored to a digit with no whitespace anywhere, so `a < b`, `1 << 4` and `0 <= n` are untouched.

patterns.comment: An explicit float suffix makes a float of anything, `1e-9f32` included.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.float.science

patterns.comment: A dot only makes a float when a digit follows it, so `1.foo()` and `0..n` stay integers.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.float.science

keyword-declaration.comment: The words that introduce something. Same split as web/assets/highlight.js DECLARE.
keyword-declaration.name: keyword.declaration.science

keyword-control.comment: Control flow plus the operators and values spelled as words. Same split as highlight.js CONTROL.
keyword-control.name: keyword.control.science

keyword-reserved.comment: Reserved for F1-F4 by TokenKind::from_word. Never an identifier, not usable today.
keyword-reserved.name: invalid.deprecated.reserved.science

function-call.comment: A name followed by `(`, looking past spaces so `map (x)` and `map(x)` read alike.
function-call.name: entity.name.function.science

type-name.comment: A capitalised word is a type. Checked before the label rule so `type Doc:` is a type and not a field.
type-name.name: entity.name.type.science

label.comment: A lowercase name followed by `:` is a named argument, a field, a parameter or a match binding.
label.name: variable.parameter.science

removed-operator.comment: `==` and `!=` were removed by syntax-revision-2 §1 and `!` begins nothing. Each is a lexer error (SC0016, SC0017, SC0001).
removed-operator.name: invalid.illegal.operator.science

operator.comment: Longest match first, exactly as lexer.rs `fn operator` does it. `?` is here because a reader arriving from Rust writes it; it is an error, but colouring it as an operator is what makes its squiggle legible.
operator.name: keyword.operator.science

extern-block.comment: `unsafe extern "C" library ...:` and its indented body. The `while` keeps the block open for every line indented past the header, which is how an indentation-delimited block is expressed in TextMate.

extern-clause.comment: Words that are keywords only inside an extern block: the header clauses of ffi-c-boundary.md §5.1-§5.2, and the `static`/`union`/`symbol`/`size`/`align` items of §1.2 and §1.4. Listed before #code so `static` and `union` are not coloured as phase-reserved words here, where they mean something.
extern-clause.name: keyword.other.extern.science
